previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with IgA multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, was admitted for worsening redness and pain in his right second toe, concerning for recurrent osteomyelitis, along with cellulitis on his left shin. MRI confirmed osteomyelitis, leading to a distal phalangectomy. Cultures from the toe were negative, but prior positive cultures for Morganella morganii guided continued IV ceftriaxone. The left leg cellulitis grew Staphylococcus epidermidis and was treated with antibiotics. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV therapy. His hemolytic anemia remained stable on prednisone, kidney function was baseline, and diabetes was well-controlled on insulin. He completed a course of IVIG for hypogammaglobulinemia. He was discharged home with plans for home antibiotic infusion, wound care, and follow-up in infectious disease, podiatry, and oncology.

microbiology.comments: NO ANTIBODY TO B. BURGDORFERI DETECTED BY EIA.  Reference Range:  No antibody detected.  Negative results do not rule out B. burgdorferi infection.  Patients in early stages of infection or on antibiotic therapy may not produce  detectable levels of antibody.  Patients with clinical history and/or  symptoms suggestive of lyme disease should be retested in 2-3 weeks.
